title: Render a responsive browser spec at every declared viewport width

facts.note: browser_spec = a `*.e2e.ts` file run by Playwright (both conditions required), or any test file whose header comments carry a journey marker (`// Train:`, `// Journey:`, `// URN: test:train:…`, `// URN: test:journey:…`). Establishing Playwright use and reading header comments needs a content observer (htmx_e2e_detector does this). A unit test merely mentioning a journey URN in a string is not a browser_spec. Necessary but not sufficient: one of the two responsive identifiers below must also hold.

Matched against tokens of the file's basename only (split on `.`, `-`, `_`), never against directory names or arbitrary substrings. Only counts together with browser_spec. Vendored/generated trees (`node_modules`, `dist`, `build`, `_generated`) are excluded.
Alternative responsive identifier to the filename token: the spec's test URN carries the `RESP` harness code; requires reading the URN from file content (htmx_e2e_detector).

fires: A Playwright-run *.e2e.ts browser spec whose test URN carries the RESP code is added or edited
A browser spec whose file basename contains a `responsive` or `resp` token is added or edited
A misnamed test file whose header carries a journey marker and whose test URN carries the RESP code is added or edited
doesNotFire: A browser spec with no RESP URN and no responsive/resp token in its file basename
A browser spec that sits in a directory named `responsive` but whose own basename and URN carry no responsive identifier
A `*.e2e.ts` file not run by Playwright and without a journey header marker
A unit test that merely mentions a journey URN inside a string
A task that mentions mobile or viewport behaviour but touches no responsive browser spec
Files under node_modules, dist, build or _generated

given: A browser spec identified as responsive: its test URN carries the RESP code, or its file basename has a `responsive`/`resp` token.
when: You write or change that spec.
then: Render the page at every viewport width declared in `atdd-bun.yaml` under `frontend.viewports` (default 375, 768, 1280).
prefer: Iterate the declared widths and set each one: `for (const width of [375, 768, 1280]) { await page.setViewportSize({ width, height: 900 }); ... expect(scrollWidth - clientWidth).toBeLessThanOrEqual(0); }`
Set widths via `page.setViewportSize({ width })`, a `viewport: { width }` option, or by iterating a list of widths (`for (const w of [...])`, `LIST.forEach`, `LIST.map`).
avoid: Picking one element of a widths list (e.g. `WIDTHS[0]`) — that renders only one width.

Measuring `scrollWidth` without passing it (directly or through a variable measured from it) to an `expect(...)`; the spec MUST do so, so the test fails when the page overflows horizontally (separate obligation, see split suggestion).
why: A screen that works on a desktop can be unusable on a phone; rendering at each declared width and asserting the document never scrolls sideways is the least that proves it fits.
evidence: htmx_e2e_detector reports no responsive-harness finding for the spec.
Reviewer sees every width in `frontend.viewports` (or default 375/768/1280) rendered via setViewportSize, a viewport option, or an iterated list.
Reviewer sees `scrollWidth`, directly or through a variable measured from it, inside an `expect(...)`.
verifier_detail: Responsive spec identification: a `RESP` test URN, or a `responsive`/`resp` token in the file name.

browser_spec: a `*.e2e.ts` file run by Playwright, or any test file whose header comments carry a journey marker (`// Train:`, `// Journey:`, `// URN: test:train:…`, `// URN: test:journey:…`), so a misnamed one is still judged. A unit test that merely mentions a journey URN in a string is not one.

Accepted width-rendering forms: `page.setViewportSize({ width })`, `viewport: { width }` option, iterating a list (`for (const w of [...])`, `LIST.forEach`, `LIST.map`); picking one element of a list renders one width.
Overflow assertion: the spec MUST pass `scrollWidth` to `expect(...)` directly or through a variable measured from it, so the test fails when the page overflows horizontally.
Vendored and generated trees (`node_modules`, `dist`, `build`, `_generated`) are never scanned.
audit: Statement note: New in the Bun/htmx browser tester, strict.
Source name/summary: A RESP spec renders at every declared viewport and asserts no horizontal overflow.

splitSuggestion.then: In a browser spec identified as responsive (a `RESP` test URN, or a `responsive`/`resp` token in its file name), pass `scrollWidth`, directly or through a variable measured from it, to an `expect(...)` so the test fails when the page overflows horizontally.

additions.text: `then` keeps only viewport coverage (S006). The scrollWidth overflow assertion (S007) is a second independent obligation; it is preserved verbatim in avoid[1], evidence[2] and verifier_detail[4], and should become its own convention tester.htmx.responsive-overflow-assertion with the same responsive-spec scope.
additions.justification: Rule 2: one obligation in `then`; source statement contains two MUSTs.

additions.text: Filename-token matching is specified as basename tokens (split on `.`, `-`, `_`), not substrings or directory names.
additions.justification: Source says 'a `responsive`/`resp` token in its file name'; this makes that observable precisely without broadening scope.
